_README: Copy to athlete.json and replace every number with your own. The values shipped here come from the author (a middle-distance runner) and are meaningless for anybody else: the heart-rate anchors are from a 2023 lactate test, the running-power bands were fitted on hand-labelled sessions, and the condition-score constants were tuned on roughly 200 days of that one person's data.

baselines._README: Personal normal. resting_hr is the median of your own resting HR on healthy days; respiration is the median sleeping respiration rate (breaths/min). The condition score deducts points for excursions ABOVE these.

classifier._README: Run classifier gates. Pace is seconds per kilometre (smaller = faster), power is watts from a running-power capable watch, HR is bpm.

load_explanation._README: How much a recent session is allowed to explain an overnight HRV drop. Load is Garmin's unitless activityTrainingLoad; for this athlete an easy jog lands near distance_km * 7-10, a quality session above 120, a race above 170. day_weights is how far back the window reaches (1 = yesterday).

condition_score._README: Weights of the condition score (0-100, deductions from 100). Caps are the maximum points any one channel may remove; pivots are where a deduction starts; lb_* are the label boundaries.

pmc._README: Banister fitness-fatigue model. ctl_days / atl_days are the exponential time constants in days (42 / 7 is the TrainingPeaks convention). season_start is where the series is seeded at zero; percentile_from skips the warm-up so 'CTL vs my own year' is not biased by the seed.

status._README: Status dashboard. acwr_safe is the acute:chronic band treated as normal; week_load_target_pct is the half-width of the weekly load target around CTL*7; all_out_* define the window after a maximal effort in which the autonomic metrics are not trusted; ctl_percentile_open is the CTL percentile the race-window verdict requires.
